Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. The present applicant has invoked the inherent power of this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C. to assail orders dated 01.10.2024 and 09.10.2024 passed by learned Additional District & Sessions Judge, Court No.1, District Varanasi in Session Trial No.1007 of 2021 (State Vs. Umesh Singh &
others), arising out of Case Crime No.359 of 2021, under Sections 498A, 304-B, 302 IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Bhelupur, District Varanasi, pending in the court of learned Additional District & Sessions Judge, Court No.1, District Varanasi.

sentences.text: While passing the order impugned, learned court below has relied upon the case of Umanath Singh and others Vs. State of U.P., in Criminal Revision No.384 of 1985, decided on February 21, 1986.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. Having considered the rival submissions advanced by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perusal of the record, it reveals that having been aggrieved with the behaviour of in-laws of his daughter opposite party no.2 (father of the deceased wife) has lodged an FIR against the husband and his family members.

After due investigation, Investigating Officer has submitted a charge sheet arraigning the applicant and his family members under Sections 498A, 304-B, 302 IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act.
5.
During pendency of the trial, accused has submitted the list of 14 witnesses, out of them only three were examined.
In furtherance thereof, three other witnesses were also requested to be examined, who are Government employees.

In view of the above, learned Additional District and Sessions Judge has passed an order dated 01.10.2024 for depositing one day salary of all the three accused as expenses so that they may be called on in witness box.
Accused has moved an application dated 08.10.2024 to the effect that the expenses may be recovered from the State Government under the provisions of law as enunciated under Section 312 Cr.P.C.

Learned court concerned, vide order dated 03.10.2024, has rejected the aforesaid application dated 08.10.2024 affirming the previous order to the effect that the accused shall deposit one day salary of all the witnesses who are expected to be called on as defence witnesses.

6. Prima facie, it appears that learned court concerned has misread and misinterpret the observation made by the Single Judge of this Court in the matter of Umanath Singh & others (supra) wherein no specific direction has been issued by the court concerned to the effect that accused has to deposit the expenses under Section 312 read with 233(2) Cr.P.C. to summon any person in the witness box.
A simple observation has been made that reasonable expenses, which is incurred upon the State Government shall be decided as per rule.

7. Having considered the provisions of law under Section 312 and 233 Cr.P.C., coordinate Bench of this Court in the matter of Krishna Kumar Pandey alias Kukku Pandey Vs. State of U.P., Case No.2109 of 2008 decided on June 17, 2008 reported in 2008(3) ALL CriR 2691 has elucidated that in sessions trial accused cannot be held liable to pay all the expenses to call upon the witnesses in the witness box.

entities.text: Krishna Kumar Pandey alias Kukku Pandey Vs. State of U.P., Case No.2109 of 2008
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
8. For ready reference, paragraph nos.15 and 16 of the aforesaid order is quoted herein below:-
"15.
But in the wisdom of the legislature this discretion has not been given to the Sessions Judge in respect of the cases triable by the Court of Sessions as in the present case.
The object is clear and bold.
The cases triable by Sessions are of heinous nature in which more stringent punishment is provided.
As such, the statutory right of defence becomes more significant and important.

Therefore, with a view that this statutory right may not get frustrated or diluted, the discretion for requiring Umesh Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163596835/
2 deposition of reasonable expenses as a condition precedent for summoning a defence witness has been done away with consciously in respect of cases of grave nature triable by Sessions.

entities.text: Umesh Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the Sessions Judge may refuse such prayer only on the ground if it appears to has been made for the purpose of vexation or delay or defeating the ends of justice.
But the reason for the same has to be recorded.

These provisions are contained under Section 233 Cr.P.C. Chapter XVIII which are as under:--
Entering upon defence.-- (1) Where the accused is not acquitted under section 232,
he shall be called upon to enter on his defence and adduce any evidence he may have in support thereof.
(2) If the accused puts in any written statement, the Judge shall file it with the record.

(3) If the accused applies for the issue of any process for compelling the attendance of any witness or the production of any document or thing, the Judge shall issue such process unless he considers, for reasons to be recorded, that such application should be refused on the ground that it is made for the purpose of vexation or delay or for defeating the ends of justice.
16.

Thus, from a study of the aforesaid provisions relating to the summoning of defence witness it is clear that as far as the Sessions Trial is concerned the provisions of the Code stands on the same footing in respect of summoning the prosecution witness viz-a-viz defence witness and there is no difference.
In other words like prosecution witnesses the defence witness in the sessions case are also to be summoned at the expenses of the State.

The only rider is that such a request made by defence can be rejected if the learned Sessions Judge finds that the request has been made for the purpose of vexation or delay or defeating the ends of justice.
A Sessions court may also take recourse in this regard to the enabling provision envisaged in Section 312 Cr.P.C. quoted hereinbefore.

Almost similar view has been taken in the following case laws:--
1.Mahe Alam Vs. State of U.P. and others, reported in 2005 Cri. L.J. 4554.
